Alex.confusing: Special actions like a wink only happen if you win the floor. My round 3 wink on Blair failed because I lost the bid, and Blair doubled down and outed me first. Being the Mouser all three rounds also felt odd when teams are meant to be re-dealt.
Alex.fun: Round 1: Blair and I didn't know we were both Meowfia, but we backed each other's fake claims and got the real Tit eggsecuted 17-3.
Alex.change: Let a special action like a wink or double-down happen even when you don't win the floor, as CAW CAW already does. Otherwise a key action can fail without you knowing.
Alex.regret: In round 2 I claimed Falcon even though a real Falcon could easily exist. Finley, the real Falcon, exposed me and I had to switch claims. I should have started with Hawk on Ellis, which my visit actually matched.

Blair.confusing: How double-down cards are entered was unclear. I first put them inside the special action, the schema rejected it, and they actually go in the top-level cards field. It was also easy to forget that my early double down still counted for score after I was winked, but not as a vote.
Blair.fun: Round 3: my Hawk egg from Alex, together with Casey's Owl report that Alex got nothing, ruled out Turkey. That let me double down with confidence, and getting winked right afterward told everyone I was right.
Blair.change: Have the app check claims against the roles in play. For example, round 2's Sphinx list showed four specific Farm roles, so a Pigeon couldn't exist, but nobody noticed. A short public summary of how many Farm roles are in play would make that kind of logic easier to use.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I claimed Pigeon even though I knew all four Farm players had named roles, so my claim was provably false and only survived because nobody checked. I also gave up on Alex and threw at Casey. I'd have done better claiming Falcon or Turkey to start a real counterclaim fight and pushing votes away from Alex.

Casey.confusing: Confusion was the most confusing part. A confused player draws cards based on their false report, so Drew's real +1 nest change in round 2 looked like proof of Blair's Pigeon claim when it was actually a side effect of the confusion. That made a public nest count, which usually counts as solid evidence, misleading.
Casey.fun: Round 3, when my Owl report on Alex and Drew's Falcon report both confirmed Blair as the real Hawk. Then Blair got winked, and the table worked out the 6-to-5 vote count together.
Casey.change: I would make the public nest-size list reflect only real egg-laying, not draws caused by confusion, or at least flag the confusion rule more clearly. As it stands, nest changes can quietly back up a false claim.
Casey.regret: In round 1, I argued that the 'one cat' explanation was simpler and pushed the table onto Drew, but Alex and Blair were both cats. I should have taken the possibility of two Meowfia seriously and thrown at Blair or Alex. Also, in round 2 I should have doubled down on Alex before speaking, since the case against him was strong.

Drew.confusing: In round 1 I lost several bids, so my visit to Alex was never actually said. I then doubled down as if the table already knew it. It wasn't obvious that words I wrote but didn't get to say counted for nothing.
Drew.fun: In round 3, counting the votes after Blair was winked: Blair's throws stopped counting, and getting Casey to throw at Alex decided the round.
Drew.change: Have the app confirm which claims and details each player has actually said aloud, so players don't assume information was shared when it wasn't.
Drew.regret: In round 2 I accepted Blair's Pigeon claim, but Pigeon should only go to extra Farm players and there were spare Farm animals. I should have pressed that, since Blair was the Sphinx. In round 1 I should have given my full story before doubling down.

Ellis.confusing: The timing of double-down wasn't clear. My first attempt silently didn't happen because I didn't win the floor, even though the special-action wording read as if it would act right away. It was also unclear whether a dead player's thrown cards count as votes against them until it played out.
Ellis.fun: Round 3, when Blair's Hawk egg, Casey's Owl report and Drew's Falcon sighting all pointed at Alex. Then Blair got winked, which confirmed it, and the whole Farm doubled down together.
Ellis.change: Let a double-down or other special action happen even when you don't win the floor, like CAW CAW does. Tying it to winning the bid makes the 'before you have spoken' window feel random.
Ellis.regret: In round 1 I argued that cats can't know each other and pushed the table onto Drew. I missed that a Mouser visiting Blair would learn she was a cat, which is exactly what Drew said. I should have taken Drew's point seriously and thrown at Blair, or at least held back my vote.

Finley.confusing: How the Floofer's hug works with other abilities, for example whether a Mouser visiting the Floofer still learns its role. I wasn't sure what anyone could have learned in Round 1.
Finley.fun: Round 3: Blair collapsed from a Wink right after exposing Alex, and the whole table doubled down on him one after another.
Finley.change: Show each player their running score and the bonus breakdown after every round, not just at the start of the next one. That would make the trade-off between doubling down and bonding easier to judge.
Finley.regret: In Round 1 I backed the "cats can't coordinate" argument and threw at Drew, the real Tit. Instead I should have pushed on Alex's claim that he wasn't confused, which nobody could check, and thrown at Blair.

review.title: The Hawk Speaks Twice
review.headline: Two cats framed the real Tit, then a dead Hawk banked the win.
review.summary: In round 1, Alex and Blair were the cats. They did not know each other, but they backed each other's fake claims and got the real Tit, Drew, eggsecuted. Both banked big, doubled scores. Alex was the Mouser again in rounds 2 and 3. He was caught both times, the second time even after he winked Blair, the Hawk who exposed him. Blair played a clever Sphinx in round 2 and doubled down as Hawk in round 3, so Blair won with 94. Every Farm player doubled down in the final round, which tripled the score totals.

rounds.recap: Drew, the real Tit, doubled down on Blair for falsely claiming Tit. Alex (Mouser) had learned that Drew was the Tit, so he knew Blair was lying. He claimed Kookaburra, said he saw Blair as the Tit, and said nobody had visited him. Drew's counter-theory needed a Mouser visiting a Floofer, which can't work because the Floofer hugs its visitors. Finley caught that flaw, and the table eggsecuted Drew.

Blair (Sphinx) chose Kookaburra and landed on Drew, which confused him. Drew's confused report showed a fake +1 egg, and Blair claimed to be the Pigeon who laid it. Alex hid his role until Finley's Falcon report forced him to claim Hawk. The table read his visit to Ellis as a Sphinx choosing Tit, and Alex was eggsecuted almost unanimously.

Alex was the only cat. Blair's Hawk egg, Casey's Owl report and Drew's Falcon report all pointed at him. Alex doubled down on Blair with a Pigeon counterclaim, then winked Blair to wipe out Blair's 4 votes. Finley and Ellis then doubled down on Alex as well, and he was eggsecuted 8 to 5.

highlights.text: Alex's Mouser visit told him Drew was the real Tit, so he could vouch for Blair, a cat he couldn't otherwise identify, with a fake Kookaburra claim.
Drew doubled down on the truth and lost, while the two liars doubled down and got paid.
Blair's Sphinx confused the Kookaburra, then claimed Pigeon to explain the fake +1 egg the confusion had created.
Alex winked Blair right after Blair's double down, which cancelled Blair's votes. The kill pointed straight at Alex, and Blair's doubled score still counted.

confusions.what: Guessed Pigeon because it was 'the most common role'. With 7 non-buffer Farm animals and at most 5 Farm players, the Pigeon is never dealt.
Treated his +1 egg as real proof that someone visited him. A confused report's egg count is wrong, so Blair's Pigeon claim was built on an egg nobody laid.
Said 'Blair's egg on Drew verifies Blair', missing that the egg came from a confused report and that the Pigeon can't be dealt. Casey also said 'I said it twice' without having spoken before.
Argued that a Mouser or House Cat visiting Blair would learn Floofer. The Floofer hugs its visitors, so they would learn nothing.
Claimed Pigeon, a role that can't be dealt this game. Nobody at the table challenged it, just as nobody challenged Blair's Pigeon claim in round 2.
His survey mentions a 'Falcon cover' falling apart, but he never claimed Falcon. He claimed Hawk.

worked: Kookaburra plus Sphinx: the Sphinx can confuse the Kookaburra on purpose, and the false egg it creates is a great bluffing opening (round 2).
Mouser role-learning let a cat find its unknown partner by elimination and cover for it, which gave round 1 a real two-cat swindle.
Hawk, Owl and Falcon cross-checks in round 3 formed a fair, solvable puzzle that three Farm players confirmed independently.
Crimson Kunzea's public, early commitment created real drama in round 1 when the truth-teller and the liars both went all in.
problems: Pigeon is listed in the pool but works as a buffer, so with 7 Farm animals it is never dealt. Players claimed it and guessed it as if it were common. Either drop it from the listed pool or state plainly that it is buffer-only.

Crimson Kunzea is too swingy. Doubled wins were most of every final score, and in round 3 four Farm players doubled down on an obvious read. Consider a cap (for example, +50% value) or limit it to one player per round.

Golden Wattle barely mattered. Meowfia gain +3 from any bond, so a handshake offer is itself a tell, as Drew pointed out, and only one bond formed all game. Hide the payoff or give Farm a reason to offer.
Role dealing repeated: Alex was the Mouser in all three rounds, and Blair was a cat twice. Check the randomizer, or avoid dealing the same player the same role in back-to-back rounds.

The engine log leaked 'no effect at tier 50' on the round 1 hug. Clean up internal debug text. Also, carried-over nests shrank to 2 cards for most players by round 3, so their only lever was the double down.
